## Settled

### Settled: the course, Sprint 0 (from the instructor's site + Blackboard, given 2026-09-14)

**Deadline: 2026-09-17, 11:59 PM.** Sprint 0 = 100 points, 9% of the course grade.
Team **Cal.diy**: Zachary Short, Zachary Bowden, Demir Batu Beynam, Julissa Hernandez,
Joshua Ko, Dylan Han. Source: `https://csci-435-se.github.io/sprint0/`. Communication is Zulip,
not GitHub.

| D | Deliverable | Where it goes | Points |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Project setup: run locally, test suite passes; screenshots + written answers | evidence in D6 | 10 |
| D2 | ≥4 GitHub issues per member (2 small/medium, 2 ambitious), required fields + labels | the issue tracker | 20 |
| D3 | Standards & guidelines doc | `docs/sprint0/standards.md` | 10 |
| D4 | AI tooling + captured logs | `ai-logs/sprint0/<github-username>/` | 5 |
| D5 | **Exactly 2 PRs per member**, on issues *someone else wrote* | the repo | 30 |
| D6 | Sprint report | `docs/sprint0/report.md` | 10 |
| D7 | Release tag `v<version>-csci435-s0` | GitHub release | 10 |
| D8 | Reflection survey (individual) | Blackboard/Zulip | 5 |

**Minimum bar:** no running app (D1), no sprint report (D6), or no merged PRs (D5) ⇒ **0 for the
whole sprint**, regardless of everything else.

**Rules that constrain how AI is used here — these bind this agent:**

- **He must be able to explain every line.** Prefer explaining and reviewing over generating;
  points are lost if he cannot explain his own PR.
- **Branch names**: `feat/issue-<n>-<slug>` or `fix/issue-<n>-<slug>`.
  **Commit messages**: the spec's own example is `feat: add dark mode toggle (#17)` —
  **Conventional Commits**, matching `AGENTS.md`, and *contradicting* the team's draft
  `standards.md` ("Add …"). The course spec and `main` agree; the draft is the outlier.
- **PRs**: link the issue with `Closes #<n>`, tests written/updated, reviewed by a teammate with
  an actual comment, CI passing (CI not required for Sprint 0). `main` is branch-protected.
- **AI logs** are captured with **SpecStory**, not written by hand.

### Settled: D1 — the app runs locally

Verified 2026-09-14 on Node 22.14.0. `./scripts/cal dev` brings it up (it starts Postgres,
ensures the database exists, then runs `yarn dev`).

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `yarn workspace @calcom/prisma db-migrate` | exit 0, 14s, **105 tables** |
| `yarn db-seed` | **41 users, 151 event types**; logins `free:free`, `pro:pro` |
| Dev server | `✓ Ready in 451ms`, listening on `:3000` |
| `GET /auth/login` | **200**, title `Login | Cal.diy` |
| `GET /pro` | **200**, title `Pro Example | Cal.diy` — the name comes from the seeded DB, so this is a full round-trip, not a static shell |
| `GET /pro/30min` | **200** |

**Known non-blocking console error:** the dev overlay shows "1 Issue" — a Service Worker
registration failure. `/sw.js` returns **404** in dev; the registration comes from
`apps/web/modules/notifications/components/WebPushContext.tsx`. Page rendering and navigation
are unaffected. Do not chase it as a regression.

**Still owed for D1:** the screenshots themselves (app running, test suite passing) have to be
taken by Zach — no agent here can capture his screen — and the written architecture answers,
which are D6 content.

### Settled: how AI logs are captured (D4)

Syllabus §16: "An AI log is the record of an AI conversation with an AI tool — the prompts,
responses, and tool used. Logs are pushed to the team's GitHub repository rather than submitted
separately, and **referenced from the related GitHub issue**." Separately, "for each issue or
sprint, include a short written rationale (in the pull request description or sprint report)
explaining how AI output was used, especially when a suggestion was modified or rejected."
So the log is the **transcript**; the rationale is a different artifact and lives in the PR/report.

**The authoritative spec is <https://csci-435-se.github.io/ai-logs/>** (read 2026-09-14) — not
`ai-logs/README.md`, which only summarises it and links a `docs/sprints.md` that exists on no
ref. Requirements, verbatim where it matters:

- Path `ai-logs/sprint<N>/<github-username>/`; filename `YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>.md`.
  Zach's GitHub login is **`zach-short`** (confirmed via `gh api user`). Tool id for this tool
  is **`claude-code`**; `claude-desktop` is the separate Claude Desktop chat app.
- The log must state **the model/tool used** ("e.g. 'Claude Sonnet 4.5 via Claude Code'"), carry
  **the full prompt and response history**, and for agentic tools **all file edits and commands
  run**. A log with "only your prompts (no AI responses), or that is clearly incomplete" does
  **not** meet the requirement. SpecStory satisfies all three: every agent turn is headed
  `_**Agent (claude-opus-5 <timestamp>)**_`, so the model is stated throughout.
- **Files pasted into a session as context** (images, PDFs, snippets) go in a folder beside the
  log with the same name minus `.md`. Report evidence such as D1 screenshots is *not* session
  context and does not belong there.
- **Each log is referenced from the related GitHub issue** as a comment, one per contributor:

  ```
  | # | Tool | Log | What AI helped with |
  ```

  with a link to the log file and the contributor's role (Implementation / Code review /
  Testing / Other). "No AI used." if none. **This is the "link" — it points at the log file,
  and it lives in an issue comment, not inside the log.**
- **At sprint end, run `specstory sync` once more** and copy the sprint's files across; a sync
  is only a snapshot of the session so far.

**SpecStory is installed** (`~/.local/bin/specstory`, v2.10.0) and — importantly — **sessions
that were never launched via `specstory run` can still be recovered**, which the course warns is
otherwise hard after the fact:

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
specstory list claude                                  # sessions for THIS directory
specstory sync -s <session-id> --output-dir <dir> --local-time-zone
```

Two gotchas, both verified 2026-09-14:

- **Sessions are bucketed by the directory the session ran in.** A session run inside
  `.claude/worktrees/<name>/` is **not** listed from the repo root — run `specstory list` from
  the same directory the session used, or it looks like the log does not exist.
- **A sync is a snapshot.** Re-run it at the end of a session, or the log stops partway.

**Before committing any transcript, scan it for secrets (R16).** SpecStory redacts by default,
but verify rather than trust: grep the file for the literal values in `.env` and for key shapes
(`ghp_`, `github_pat_`, `sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}`, `AKIA`, `BEGIN … PRIVATE KEY`). Done for the
2026-09-14 log: zero hits.

# Sprint 0 Deliverables Summary

## D1 — Project Setup (Team)
**Requires:** Clone repo, follow STUDENTS.md setup guide, run test suite, read architecture docs, answer questions about system functionality, components, technologies, organization, and contribution workflow.

**Evidence:** Screenshots of app running locally and tests passing; written answers included in sprint report.

**Submission:** Evidence in D6 (sprint report).

---

## D2 — Feature Backlog (Team)
**Requires:** Each member proposes minimum 4 GitHub Issues (more encouraged), comprising "2 small or medium" and "2 ambitious" features per person.

**Issue requirements:** Title, Summary, User story, Rough scope, Source.

**Required labels:** `scope: small`, `scope: medium`, `scope: large`, `scope: xl`, `type: feature`, `type: improvement`, `type: bug`.

**Submission:** GitHub Issues in team repository, linked from sprint report.

---

## D3 — Standards & Guidelines Document (Team)
**Requires:** Review project's CONTRIBUTING.md, AGENTS.md, linter configs, and existing Definition of Done. Document team's adopted or adapted standards across sections:
- Coding conventions
- Branching and commit conventions
- Pull request process
- Testing expectations
- AI tool use
- Definition of Done

**Submission:** `docs/sprint0/standards.md` (or equivalent format) pushed to repository.

---

## D4 — AI Tooling Setup (Team)
**Requires:** Review project AI files; each team member selects agentic tool (Claude Code recommended); set up AI log capture via SpecStory or browser extensions; log all sessions starting day one.

**Tools mentioned:** Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, OpenAI Codex CLI, Gemini CLI.

**Log storage:** `ai-logs/sprint0/<your-github-username>/` with summary in D6.

**Submission:** No separate deliverable; evidence and usage summary in D6.

---

## D5 — Code Changes and Pull Requests (Individual)
**Requires:** Each member opens **exactly 2 pull requests** implementing issues written by others (not self-authored). Follow branch-based workflow.

**Branch naming:** `feat/issue-<number>-<description>` or `fix/issue-<number>-<description>`.

**PR requirements:**
- Link to GitHub issue (`Closes #<number>`)
- Clear description explaining what and why
- Tests written or updated
- Reviewed by at least one teammate (review comment required)
- CI passing (optional for Sprint 0)

**Submission:** All PRs in GitHub repository, links in D6.

---

## D6 — Sprint Report (Team)
**Requires:** One report per team with sections:
- Team (name, members with GitHub usernames, project/repo link)
- Project overview (answering D1 questions)
- Feature backlog summary (count, themes, top 3–5, links to issues)
- Standards document summary (key conventions adopted, link to standards.md)
- Completed PRs (table: title, issue link, author, reviewer(s), status, description)
- AI tool usage (per member: tools, task types, sessions, link to ai-logs folder, observations)
- Release (tag name and link)
- Risks and challenges
- Sprint 1 ideas

**Format:** Markdown (`docs/sprint0/report.md`), PDF, or Word (.docx).

**Submission:** Push to repository by Sep 17, 11:59 PM.

---

## D7 — Sprint Release (Team)
**Requires:** Create Git tag with format `v<current-version>-csci435-s0` (do not bump version). Example: if current is `v2.17.2`, tag as `v2.17.2-csci435-s0`. If no prior releases, use `v0.1.0-csci435-s0`.

**Commands:**
```
git tag v<version>-csci435-s0
git push origin v<version>-csci435-s0
```

Create GitHub release from tag with brief description of changes.

**Submission:** Link to GitHub release in D6 by Sep 17, 11:59 PM.

---

## D8 — Reflection Survey (Individual)
**Requires:** Each team member complete individual survey reflecting on Sprint 0 process and AI usage.

**Submission:** Via Blackboard/Zulip link by Sep 17, 11:59 PM.

---

## Deadline
**All deliverables due Sep 17, 11:59 PM** (except Lightning Talk on Sep 22).

---

## Grading
- D1: 10 pts
- D2: 20 pts (up to 5 extra credit)
- D3: 10 pts
- D4: 5 pts
- D5: 30 pts (15 per PR × 2)
- D6: 10 pts
- D7: 10 pts
- D8: 5 pts
- **Total: 100 pts (9% of course grade)**

**Minimum bar:** App must run, sprint report submitted, PRs merged; otherwise 0 for entire sprint.

# /handoff

The ledger is **what is true**. The board is what is next. Keep them apart: a fact in the board
rots the moment its item is done.

## Reading it

Read it first, every session, before the board and before any code. Its Settled sections are
closed — **do not re-ask anything recorded there.** Its claims are leads, not facts: re-verify
before building on one, and record your verification with its own date and citation rather than
the original's.

## Appending a step

**Take the next free number by reading the file.** Another session may have taken the one a doc
predicted. **Do not edit a step you did not write** — append a correction as a new step, so the
wrong claim stays findable, marked wrong, with the disproof beside it.

A step names: what changed, why, what is now fixed, which questions it answered, and what is
left owed. It is addressable forever — "HANDOFF 24" is how everything else refers to that work.

`personal-config handoff step` does that read for you: it reports the next free number, the
ledger's modification time, and what a step has to name. It cannot *reserve* the number — only
writing would — so re-read the file immediately before you append.

## Editing a standing section

Environment, Settled, Code map, Invariants, Known facts are edited in place when they go stale,
never appended to. Two rules hold everywhere in this file:

- **Absolute dates only.** `2026-09-15`, never "today" or "recently". This is read months later
  by an agent with no idea when it was written.
- **Every claim carries a citation** — `file:line`, a commit, a migration name, or the command
  that produced it. A claim with no citation is a guess and will be treated as one.

**Run every gate command once before writing it into Environment.** A command in a doc that has
never been run in this repo is a trap for every session after you.

# /passoff

**The single highest-leverage artifact there is.** The next agent will not see this
conversation, this reasoning, or this context. A prompt that assumes any of it produces a
session that rediscovers what you already knew.

Nine parts, in this order. Skip one only when it is genuinely empty, and say so.

1. **Title.** Imperative, naming the change, not the area. *"Drag the week grid: windows edited
   where they are drawn"*, not *"week grid work"*.
2. **The header line.** `**Model: <tier>. Lane <X>. Waits on <what>.**` Plus the worktree
   instruction when the item needs its own.
3. **Orientation.** Who they are picking up, what to read first and in what order, and the
   session rules restated **inline** — not by reference. A prompt is pasted alone, and a rule
   one file away is a rule that does not arrive.
4. **Why this exists**, in product terms. This is what lets the next agent make a hundred small
   judgment calls the prompt does not cover.
5. **What is fixed.** *"Read these before changing anything; do not relitigate them."* The
   verified facts with citations, the invariants, the house precedent to copy rather than
   reinvent, the constraint that makes this smaller than it looks. This section is where this
   session's reading is **banked** instead of re-paid.
6. **Do these, in order.** Numbered, each carrying its reason and its constraint. A step that
   says only what to do gets done differently than intended.
7. **Ask before building.** The named decisions that are the owner's, each with what makes it a
   real question. Say explicitly that both are their calls, and that either answer may be no.
8. **Not in scope, whoever asks.** The negative list, named. It survives a persuasive
   mid-session argument in a way that an unstated boundary does not.
9. **Hand back.** The literal gate commands that must be green, what the owner should do and
   see, and the commit step.

`personal-config passoff next` prints the next `OPEN` item with its prompt and its model line,
and warns when something already in flight owns one of the same files; `personal-config passoff
claim <n>` marks the row `IN FLIGHT` and dates it. Neither writes the prompt — that is this
skill's work.

**A prompt rots the moment it is executed.** The ledger step is the truth; the prompt is the
ask. Never paste a prompt marked done — a fresh session would build it again.

```text
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Redact two things from the Sprint 0 AI transcripts before they reach a public repo:
a live Zulip invite token, and the full class roster pasted from the instructor's announcement.

Idempotent — safe to run on every commit during a history replay.
"""
import glob
import io
import re
import sys

TOKEN = re.compile(r"https://csci-435-se\.zulipchat\.com/join/[A-Za-z0-9]+/?")
ROSTER = re.compile(r"Teams\s*:\s*1\.\s*Actual Budget:.*?[name redacted]", re.S)

TOKEN_SUB = "[zulip invite link redacted]"
ROSTER_SUB = "[class roster redacted — 36 student names across 6 teams]"

def main() -> int:
    changed = 0
    for path in sorted(glob.glob("ai-logs/sprint0/**/*.md", recursive=True)):
        original = io.open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
        redacted = ROSTER.sub(ROSTER_SUB, TOKEN.sub(TOKEN_SUB, original))
        if redacted != original:
            io.open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(redacted)
            print(f"redacted {path}")
            changed += 1
    print(f"files changed: {changed}")
    return 0

if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```
</details></tool-use>
